name: Woebot
summary: AI-powered mental health chatbot using CBT to support depression, anxiety, stress, and mood tracking
description: Woebot is an evidence-based conversational agent that offers 24/7 mental health support using Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), mood tracking, journaling, and guided conversations. Designed to deliver instant, on-demand emotional support and self-help tools, Woebot has been studied in randomized trials showing reductions in depression and anxiety symptoms after short-term use.
patient_summary: Woebot is a chat-based, AI–powered mental health tool you can use any time for mood tracking, guided exercises, and emotional check-ins. It’s helpful for managing mild to moderate depression or anxiety, stress, and daily mental-health maintenance. It’s not a replacement for professional therapy if you have severe mental illness or crisis—use it as a supplement or stepping stone.

clinical_trials.outcome: Significant reduction in depression symptom scores (PHQ-9) after 2 weeks of daily use compared to control group

linked_conditions.context: Woebot has been shown in randomized trials to reduce depressive symptoms after 2 weeks of use. Can be used as a supplemental self-help tool for mild to moderate depression, but not a replacement for therapy or medication for severe depression.
Conversational CBT and daily check-ins help reduce anxiety and stress symptoms. Helpful for mild/moderate GAD as part of a broader mental-health plan.
Regular use over weeks associated with reductions in perceived stress and burnout in observational use. Best combined with other stress-management practices (sleep, therapy, lifestyle).

contraindications: Not a substitute for professional mental health treatment
Not appropriate as sole intervention for moderate-severe depression with suicidal ideation or psychosis
May not handle crisis situations adequately (self-harm, suicide risk)
Users with trauma or severe psychiatric disorders should seek in-person therapy first

efficacy_data.comparison_data: Compared to control group receiving information-only intervention
efficacy_data.patient_text: In a randomized trial, people who used Woebot daily for two weeks reported a statistically significant decrease in depressive symptoms compared with those who did not. Others reported reduced stress and improved emotional resilience after longer use.

exclusions: Severe depression with suicidal ideation or self-harm risk

data_shared: Aggregated and anonymized usage analytics with service providers
privacy_rating.certification: Meets standard privacy and security practices (as described by Woebot Health)

sections.heading: What Woebot Does
sections.text: Woebot is an AI-powered mental health chatbot that uses principles of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), mindfulness, and mood tracking. Through daily (or on-demand) conversations, mood check-ins, and guided exercises, Woebot helps users identify thought patterns, regulate emotions, reflect on mood, and build self-help skills—all via a friendly, conversational interface.

sections.heading: How Well Does It Work?
sections.metric: Depression symptom reduction (2-week RCT) + stress & resilience (8-week observational)
sections.text: In the first randomized controlled trial of Woebot, college students with depression or anxiety who used the app daily for 2 weeks reported a significant reduction in depressive symptoms compared to a control group. In an 8-week observational study (Woebot-LIFE), working adults reported significantly less perceived stress, lower burnout, and improved resilience.
sections.patient_text: Many users say they feel less depressed, less anxious, and more capable of coping with stress after a few weeks of regular use. Consistent use seems to produce the most benefit.

sections.heading: Who Should Use Woebot?
sections.text: Woebot is best for people who:
items: Experience mild to moderate depression or anxiety
Want an accessible, 24/7 self-help tool they can use from anywhere
Prefer flexible, conversational support instead of structured courses
Want to build daily mental-health habits like mood tracking or self-reflection
Need something private, low-cost, and easy to integrate into daily life
not_recommended: People with severe mental illness (severe depression, active suicidal thoughts, psychosis)
Those needing formal therapy, medication, or crisis intervention
Users expecting long-term therapy or deep trauma work

items.description: Daily or on-demand conversational check-ins where Woebot helps you examine thought patterns, challenge unhelpful thinking, and use CBT strategies to reframe and cope.
items.evidence: Used in RCT and observational studies showing symptom reduction in depression and stress.

items.evidence: Self-monitoring is a common element in many effective digital mental health interventions; helps increase self-awareness and adherence.

items.evidence: CBT, mindfulness, and psychoeducation are evidence-based practices for mild/moderate anxiety and depression.

items.evidence: High accessibility and ease of use increase engagement and may improve adherence compared to traditional therapy in early stages.

sections.heading: Privacy & Data Security
sections.summary: Woebot follows standard privacy and security practices. Data is encrypted; app is GDPR/CCPA compliant. Users can export or delete data on request.
items: Encryption of account and conversation data
Anonymized or aggregated analytics — no sale of personal data to advertisers
User control over optional mood journaling and data export
Does not claim HIPAA compliance — not suitable for formal clinical documentation
Safe-use policy: offers resources if user expresses suicidal ideation or crisis (but not a replacement for a crisis hotline or therapist)
data_collected: Conversation logs (text), mood and journaling entries
Device and app metadata (OS version, device type)

sections.heading: How to Start Using Woebot
steps: Download Woebot from the App Store or Google Play, or visit the official website.
Create a free account with email/login credentials.
Complete the onboarding mood assessment to help tailor conversation style.
Start daily check-ins — even 5 minutes a day can help build a habit.
Use mood tracking or journaling to log feelings, stressors, or trigger events.
Try guided CBT exercises or mindfulness practices when feeling anxious, stressed, or low.
If premium features exist and you find value in them, consider upgrading for additional content.
tips: Use it regularly — consistency improves results more than session length.
Be honest in moods and entries for better self-awareness over time.
Treat it as a supplement — not a replacement for in-person therapy if you need it.
Use the app as a tool, not a crutch — combine with healthy habits (sleep, exercise, social support).
common_mistakes: Expecting instant dramatic change — mental health improvements often develop over weeks.
Using only when feeling very unwell — regular check-ins help build resilience.
Assuming Woebot can handle crises alone — seek professional help if in crisis.
Ignoring data privacy—delete or export data if needed.

items.comparison: Structured meditation and mindfulness training — better for stress, focus, sleep, and building a meditation habit over time. Woebot is more conversational and CBT-oriented.
Great for relaxation, sleep stories, and guided meditations. Woebot is better for mood tracking, emotional support, and CBT-based conversation.

faqs.a: Yes. Woebot offers a free tier that includes chat-based support, mood tracking, journaling, and guided exercises. Some advanced features may require a paid plan, but core functionality remains free.

faqs.q: Can Woebot replace therapy or medication?
faqs.a: No. Woebot is designed as a self-help support tool for mild to moderate mental health symptoms. It’s not a substitute for professional therapy or medication in cases of severe depression, suicidal ideation, psychosis, or other serious mental health conditions.

faqs.q: Does Woebot really work for depression or anxiety?
faqs.a: There is clinical evidence (an RCT) showing that two weeks of daily Woebot use reduced depressive symptoms in college students compared to an information-only control. Other observational studies suggest reductions in stress and improvements in resilience over longer-term use. Results vary by user, and consistent use seems to improve benefits.

faqs.q: Is my data private and secure with Woebot?
faqs.a: Woebot uses encryption and follows standard privacy regulations (GDPR/CCPA). They do not sell personal data to advertisers, and you can request data export or deletion. However, the app is not HIPAA-compliant, so data stored in Woebot should not be treated as clinical records.

faqs.q: Can Woebot help in a mental health crisis?
faqs.a: No. Woebot is not a crisis intervention or suicide-prevention service. If you are experiencing suicidal thoughts, self-harm, or a mental health crisis, you should seek immediate help from a licensed mental health provider or crisis hotline.
